newsitem.title: USA: Brooke files slate for RJR board.
newsitem.headline: Brooke files slate for RJR board.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd said it has nominated a slate of directors to the board of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp that includes chairman Bennett LeBow.
The nine-member slate will seek an immediate spinoff of RJR's 80.5 percent-owned Nabisco Holdings Corp subsidiary, according to a letter obtained by Reuters.
The letter was addressed to RJR and signed by LeBow.
Liggett Group chairman and chief exeuctive officer Ronald Fulford also was named as a nominee. Liggett is a tobacco subsidiary of Brooke.
Other nominees are Liggett board member Rouben Chakalian, Ronald Bernstein, Arnold Burns, David Friedman, Richard Lampen, Barry Ridings and William Starbuck, the letter said.

LeBow teamed up last year with investor Carl Icahn in an unsuccessful fight to oust the RJR board and force an immediate spinoff. The two investors split up after the April defeat and Icahn filed his own slate on Monday.
"We are already in the tobacco business and we have our own views on how to resolve tobacco litigation," a Brooke spokesman said when asked why LeBow nominated his own slate apart from Icahn.
LeBow's move came on the last day that shareholders are permitted to file board slates for the company's 1997 annual shareholders meeting.
LeBow holds about a 1.3 percent stake in RJR, according to a source who did not want to be identified.
Icahn, who holds a 7.3 percent stake, on Monday nominated a slate to be led by Thomas Rattigan, a former executive with PepsiCo Bottling International and G. Heileman Brewing Co.

Earlier this year, Brooke Group broke from the rest of the tobacco industry and agreed to settle a class action suit as well as lawsuits from states that are seeking to recoup health care costs of smokers.
